paragraphs: Children in care in Morecambe are looked after by Lancashire County Council's fostering service and by independent agencies, including those shown above. Morecambe is part of the Lancaster district, and the council's agency foster care market position statement of April 2025 names Lancaster, with Preston, West Lancashire and Burnley, as one of the four districts with the most requests for homes that are hard to find. Together those four made up 69% of the council's requests to agencies in 2024-25.

The same statement shows who most needs a home: children over 11 were more than half of all requests, brothers and sisters who should stay together were 14%, and many children have complex social and emotional needs. The council has run campaigns for both groups. In 2021 it said nearly 60% of children in care in Lancashire were aged over 10, and in 2022 it appealed urgently for carers who could take sibling groups.

To foster for Lancashire you need to be over 21, with no upper age limit, and to live in or close to the county. You do not need to drive or hold formal qualifications. In March 2024 the council put forward an extra £960,000 for carers' allowances and fees, and in 2025 it said it had raised allowances again because of rising costs. New carers take the Skills to Foster course, join an induction academy and a mentoring scheme, and have support day and night. The council lists Lancaster, Wyre and North Fylde as an area for its informal 'talk to the team' events.

Lancashire is also one of five north west councils behind Foster with us, a recruitment hub launched in July 2024 that offers a buddy scheme and the Mockingbird model, where a hub home supports a group of nearby foster families. If you live in Morecambe, talk to the council and to two or three of the agencies above before you decide.
